# Introduction

The Full Random Effects Model (FREM) methodology requires a specific restructuring of both the NONMEM control stream and the underlying dataset. Continuous and categorical covariates must be converted into dummy "observations" so their variability and correlation can be estimated alongside the structural parameters via a unified covariance matrix.

`createFREMmodel()` does that transformation: it takes a base model and its data set and writes the FREM control stream and data set NONMEM needs.

# How createFREMmodel Works Under the Hood
Rather than adding every covariate at once, `createFREMmodel()` builds the model one covariate at a time. It first writes a minimal FREM model from the first covariate in your `covariates` argument, rewriting the `$INPUT`, `$DATA`, `$PK` and `$ERROR` blocks for that one covariate. It then works through the rest, calling `updateFREMmodel()` for each - the function that adds covariates to an existing FREM model, covered in [its own deep dive](Part3-deep-dive-updateFREMmodel.html) - so every step is the same operation.

# 1. Setup and Paths

First, load the package and define the paths to your base model and original clinical dataset.

`createFREMmodel()` writes into `modDevDir` by default, and stops rather than overwrite an existing file with the same `fremModName`. This vignette writes into a temporary directory instead.

```{r setup}
library(PMXFrem)

# Define paths to example data and converged models
modDevDir <- system.file("extdata", "SimNeb", package = "PMXFrem")
ffemDataFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimNeb/DAT-2-MI-PMX-2-onlyTYPE2-new.csv", package = "PMXFrem")

# Create a temporary directory for all generated outputs
td <- tempdir()
```

# 2. What the Base Model Needs

`createFREMmodel()` starts from a converged base model: its control stream, its `.ext` file and the data set it was fitted to.

- **The parameters' IIVs in a final `$OMEGA BLOCK(N)`.** The FREM covariates are correlated with the random effects in that block, so it must be the last `$OMEGA` record (`SAME` records aside). `numSkipOm` counts the OMEGAs before it - IIVs you do not want correlated with the covariates, or an IIV on the residual error - and must match the model; `createFREMmodel()` stops and says so if it does not. It cannot be deduced from a base model, so you always give it.
- **The number of structural THETAs is read from the `.ext`.** `numNonFREMThetas` only needs to be given when there is no `.ext`.
- **An estimation method suited to FREM.** Before it builds anything, `createFREMmodel()` reads the base model's `$ESTIMATION` records and warns when they are not: use `IMP` or `IMPMAP` (`SAEM` cannot handle missing covariate values correctly), with `NITER` of at least 150, and `PHITYPE=1` so the results can be post-processed. These are warnings, not errors: `run30` below uses `NITER=50`, and the warning appears.

MU referencing of the structural parameters is not required. The covariate parts `createFREMmodel()` writes are MU-referenced (`useMuModeling = TRUE`, the default).

The example model, `run30`, shows both: two OMEGAs - an IIV on the residual error and a fixed IIV on `D1` - before the final `$OMEGA BLOCK(3)`, so `numSkipOm = 2`; and the `$INPUT` that `cstrKeepCols` below refers to.

```{r show_base, comment=''}
base <- readLines(file.path(modDevDir, "run30.mod"))
records <- grep("^[$]", base)
# Print every record of one kind, continuation lines included
show <- function(rec) {
  for (s in grep(paste0("^[$]", rec), base)) {
    cat(base[s:(c(records[records > s], length(base) + 1)[1] - 1)], sep = "\n")
  }
}
show("INPUT")
show("OMEGA")
```

# 3. Choosing the Covariates

We need to decide which covariates to include and how they should be handled. In FREM, continuous covariates can be modeled as-is or log-transformed, while categorical covariates must be identified so they can be binarized into dummy variables.

`cstrKeepCols` lists the columns of the original data set - the dose and observation records - that the FREM data set keeps; the covariate records `createFREMmodel()` adds need none of them. Name them as the base model's `$INPUT` names them - the column names in the data file do not count - and include every data item `$PK` and `$ERROR` use, here `FOOD`. A column the base model marks `=DROP` cannot be kept.

```{r define_covariates}
# Define the complete list of covariates to include
frem_covariates <- c("AGE", "WT", "SEX", "RACEL")

# Identify categorical and log-transformed covariates
categorical_covs <- c("RACEL", "SEX")
log_transform_covs <- c("WT")

# The columns of the data set the FREM data set keeps, by their $INPUT names
keep_cols <- c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "EVID", "RATE", "FOOD", "DV")
```

## Dichotomous covariates

`bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE` recodes two-level categorical covariates from
`1`/`2` - how many data sets code sex - to `0`/`1`, which makes `0` the
reference level and the covariate effect the difference from it. Without it,
a `1`/`2`-coded covariate stops `createFREMmodel()` with an error asking for
`0`/`1` (`allowNon01 = TRUE` lets it through unchanged).

The covariate's mean THETA moves with the coding. Recoded, `SEX` becomes
`SEX_2` - `1` for level 2, `0` for level 1 - and its mean THETA `TV_SEX_2` is
the proportion of subjects at level 2. A FREM model on the original `1`/`2`
values, such as one from PsN, has a mean THETA exactly 1 higher; the model is
the same.

# 4. Generating the Model

We pass our specifications into `createFREMmodel()`. `quiet = TRUE` silences the progress messages, not the warnings: the one about `NITER` appears below.

```{r execute_create}
generated_files <- createFREMmodel(
  modName = "run30",
  modDevDir = modDevDir,
  ffemDataFile = ffemDataFile,
  outputDir = td,
  fremModName = "run30_FREM",

  # Covariate Instructions
  covariates = frem_covariates,
  catCovs = categorical_covs,
  logtCovs = log_transform_covs,

  # The OMEGAs before the final $OMEGA BLOCK
  numSkipOm = 2,

  # Dataset formatting
  cstrKeepCols = keep_cols,
  bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

# 5. Understanding the Output

`createFREMmodel()` has now generated the newly expanded `.mod` and `.csv` files. Both are read back from disk below.

## The Generated Dataset
The original dataset has been vertically expanded. For every subject, covariate records (`EVID = 2`) have been appended, one per covariate, holding the covariate's value in the `DV` column - log-transformed for `WT`, as asked - and identified by the new `FREMTYPE` column. Because we used `bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE`, `SEX` appears as `0` or `1`.

```{r show_data}
# Read the generated dataset
frem_data <- read.csv(generated_files$data)

# The first 15 rows: the original records, followed by the covariate records
head(frem_data, n = 15)
```

## The Final Model Control Stream
The control stream is substantially different. The `$PK` block now handles the structural `ETA`s alongside the covariate means, and the `$ERROR` block routes the dummy observations (via `FREMTYPE`) to their respective equations. Finally, a large `$OMEGA BLOCK` is appended to estimate the covariances.

A few things carry over from the base model:

- **The `$THETA` records keep their bounds** - `(0, ...)` on `TVCL` - with the base model's final estimates from the `.ext` as initial values. An estimate sitting on a bound is moved just inside it, with a message naming the THETA, since NM-TRAN needs an initial value strictly inside its bounds.
- **The `$TABLE` records are kept**, fitted to the FREM data set: data items it does not carry are left out (a message names them; add them to `cstrKeepCols` to keep them), `FREMTYPE` is added, and the table file is renamed so the base run's tables are not overwritten - `xptab30` becomes `xptab30_run30_FREM` here, or `xptab31` if the FREM model were called `run31`.

```{r show_model, comment=''}
# Read the generated NONMEM control stream and print it in its entirety
frem_mod <- readLines(generated_files$model)
cat(frem_mod, sep = "\n")
```

`run30_FREM.mod` is ready to run in NONMEM.

# 6. Choices createFREMmodel Makes for You

Some behaviour is decided rather than derived; it is stated here so the results are not a surprise. Each default can be changed through the argument named.

- **A covariate's mean THETA is fixed when no subject lacks a value** for it, and estimated otherwise (`fixTheta = TRUE`, the default). A missing value on some records of a subject that has a value elsewhere does not count: the FREM data set takes each subject's first non-missing value.
- **Subjects without any observation are left out** of the FREM data set - those with only dose records, for example - since they inform no estimate (`keepDoseOnlySubjects = FALSE`). Newer PsN versions do the same, so the two FREM data sets agree.
- **The base model's `IGNORE` / `ACCEPT` lists are applied** as NM-TRAN applies them, before anything is summarised. `=`, `.EQ.`, `.NE.` and `/=` compare the values as written in the data file - so `1.0` does not equal `1` - while `.EQN.`, `.NEN.` and the ordering operators compare numbers.
- **A single-character `IGNORE` (`IGNORE=@`, `IGNORE=C`) is not applied.** When it can only remove the header line - the usual case - nothing is said; when it could remove data records too, a warning asks you to filter the data first or use an `IGNORE=(list)`.

# 7. Base Models with Dropped Columns

Real base models rarely use every column of their data set: dates and subject identifiers are typically marked `=DROP` (or `=SKIP`) in `$INPUT`. `$INPUT` still names every column of the data file in order, so `createFREMmodel()` reads them by position, applies the `IGNORE` / `ACCEPT` lists - which may refer to a dropped column - and then removes the dropped columns. Columns after the last `$INPUT` item are ignored, with a message naming them.

To show it, take a copy of `run30` and its data, add a visit-date column, and drop it together with two existing columns:

```{r drop_example}
dropDir <- file.path(td, "drop-example")
dir.create(dropDir, showWarnings = FALSE)
file.copy(file.path(modDevDir, c("run30.mod", "run30.ext")), dropDir, overwrite = TRUE)

# The data with a visit date as its last column
dat <- read.csv(ffemDataFile)
dat$VDATE <- "2026-01-01"
dropData <- file.path(dropDir, "data.csv")
write.csv(dat, dropData, row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

# $INPUT: drop STUDYID and DAY, and name the new column, dropped
mod <- readLines(file.path(dropDir, "run30.mod"))
input <- grep("^\\$INPUT", mod):(grep("^\\$DATA", mod) - 1)
mod[input] <- sub(" STUDYID ", " STUDYID=DROP ", mod[input])
mod[input] <- sub(" DAY ", " DAY=DROP ", mod[input])
mod[max(input)] <- paste(mod[max(input)], "VDATE=DROP")
writeLines(mod, file.path(dropDir, "run30.mod"))
cat(mod[input], sep = "\n")
```

```{r drop_create}
drop_files <- createFREMmodel(
  modName = "run30", modDevDir = dropDir, ffemDataFile = dropData,
  outputDir = dropDir, fremModName = "run30_FREM",
  covariates = c("AGE", "WT"), numSkipOm = 2,
  cstrKeepCols = keep_cols, quiet = TRUE
)
grep("^\\$INPUT", readLines(drop_files$model), value = TRUE)
```

One more `$INPUT` form is handled: a `label=synonym` item such as `CP=DV` is read as the reserved one of the two names, `DV`, and either name may be used in `covariates`, `cstrKeepCols` and the `IGNORE` lists.
